x: In the long jump our man, Clemens (who also won the Club handicap) jumped 21 ft. 3 ins., but was beaten by an inch by J. Simpson, the Manchester University and L.A.C. athlete.
Clemens also made a good effort in the long jump, but could not get placed. Unfortunately, business prevented us from having Dunckley's assistance, and next year we shall make a better show.

A team consisting of Tosh, Scrimshaw, Williams (J.S.), Powter, Gratte, Clemens, Kench, and Ford (A.J.) made up the club team. The start from Baker Street was not at all encouraging, as the rain was descending in torrents, accompanied by plenty of lightning and thunder.
On this evening our representatives, Clemens and Fleming, won the S.A.A.L. Inter-Club Long Jump Competition, and so earned the Club's congratulations.

The Long Jump saw us gain the first two places through the agency of Clemens and Fleming, although Basford in winning the club Long Jump Handicap did so well that it was a pity he did not count in the match event.
Clemens won the Long Jump title with a fine jump of 22ft. 4½in. In the final of the half-mile Scrimshaw, although beating 1min. 57sec. for the distance, was only placed fourth.

Powell was a reserve — a similar position to that filled by Clemens, our Long-jumper and the Southern champion, in the match versus France. Congratulations to these men upon the high honour bestowed upon them.

Scrimshaw, Tosh, Clemens, Holder, Allum, Michael, Ford, Kench, Tame, Basford and Jarvis all performed creditably in the highest class without being able to claim one of the first four places which alone carry points to the Club's credit.
The L.A.C.'s long jumpers both did excellently and although Clemens made the creditable jump of 21ft. 2¼in. he could only obtain third place.

In the Southern championships held at Southend, Clemens, Footer and Scrimshaw distinguished themselves. Clemens was placed second in the Long Jump with a fine leap of 21ft. 8½in., which gains an A.A.A. standard medal; while Footer was three seconds inside A.A.A. standard (14 min. 50 sec). in finishi…
Clemens (2nd Southern Championship). Both have beaten A.A.A. standard and so earned their Club Honours Badges.

Clemens, who has gone to Manchester to take up a business appointment. Clemens has attained very high honours at Long Jumping, having been selected as a reserve for International competition, and we shall certainly miss him.
Since Clemens moved to Manchester, we have been without an outstanding long jumper; although Gray proved in our last match of the season that he has great potentialities.
